**Spooky Bonus – Addictive, Relaxing, and Full of Charm 👻**

I picked up *Spooky Bonus* by Grey Alien Games to play with my wife, and it quickly turned into one of those games where “just one more level” turns into late nights without even realizing it.

The match-3 gameplay is incredibly smooth and satisfying. It’s easy to pick up, but it keeps you hooked with clever level design and a great sense of progression. With **100 unique levels**, there’s always something new to work through, and it never feels repetitive.

One of the standout features is being able to **decorate your spooky house and yard**. It’s not just cosmetic either — the decorations actually give you **useful bonuses** that help during gameplay, which adds a really fun layer of strategy.

There’s also a good mix of features that keep things interesting:

* 13 fun bonus items (garlic bombs, silver bullets, and more)
* 6 multi-level powerups to unlock and upgrade
* Choice between **Relaxed mode** or **Timed mode**, depending on your mood
* A unique spooky atmosphere with great visuals and classical-style music

Overall, this is a **chill but highly addictive puzzle game** that’s perfect to unwind with — especially if you enjoy playing alongside someone. We had a great time with it, and it’s definitely one of those hidden gems that deserves more attention.

Highly recommended if you enjoy relaxing match-3 games with a spooky twist 🎃

Визуально приятная и не сложная (даже играя на время невозможно или почти невозможно застопориться) игра жанра три-в-ряд. Не сложная игра - очень правильное определение, точно характеризующее игру, особенно если сравнить с такой известной игрой этого же жанра как PuzzleQuest. Я недавно её прошёл, вернее, почти прошёл (последнего босса так и не смог победить) и вот ощущения невероятной лёгкости этой игры я особенно ощутил именно на контрасте с PuzzleQuest. Пускай эти две игры довольно сильно отличаются друг от друга, но определённо, если одна игра нацелена чуть ли не на хардкорщиков (думаю не так много игроков прошло PuzzleQuest), то вот Spooky Bonus нацелена на самую широкую аудиторию, так как акцентирует главным образом на двух своих элементах. Первым является очень приятная «картинка», начиная с фона и заканчивая самими иконками фигурок которые мы передвигаем (а так же их анимация). Во-вторых, лёгкость игры создаёт релаксирующую обстановку, когда игра никак не напрягает и можно её совмещать с прослушиванием аудиокниг или чего-то подобного.

Визуальная составляющая. Тема беспроигрышная, конечно – Хэллоуин. Реализация получилась хорошей. Красивый фон игры, неплохая картинка на которой мы обустраиваем свой собственный дом различными предметами Хэллоуина. Ну и конечно сами иконки объектов, которые мы переставляем.  Они получились особенно красивыми. И конечно и они являются темой Хэллоуина: гроб, летучая мышь, кукла по типу Вуду, большущий чан, свеча, череп, чёрная кошка. Нарисованы эти иконки очень красиво. В общем, к визуальной стороне дела у меня претензий нет, так как мне всё очень понравилось.

Звуковая тема, скорее всего многим покажется скучной и однообразной, но это беда всех подобных небольших проект – дешёвая музыкальная тема. Но вот звуки уже более приятны уху, т.е. звук складывающихся или передвигающихся этих самых иконок, которые мы выстраиваем три в ряд. В совокупности с визуальной частью игры, в итоге мы имеем приятные и глазу и уху игру данного жанра, но которая старается (хотя бы старается!) не копировать своих коллег, особенно в части не быть похожей на мобильные аналоги. Если сравнивать с другой игрой этого жанра – Heroes of Hellas - у обсуждаемой игры это получилось намного лучше, чем у Heroes of Hellas.

Итак, выглядит и звучит игра, особенно для цены в 100-150 рублей очень даже хорошо. Игра довольно лёгкая и эти 100 уровней пролетят за пару дней. Поэтому последнее, что хотелось бы здесь отметить, это бонусы, т.е. специальные объекты которые  работают по принципу «удара по площади», благодаря чему уничтожается заметное количество объектов на карте. Таких бонусов в игре много и что самое главное, их можно улучшать. На те деньги, что мы собираем, можно купить улучшение, правда не сразу, а как только такое предложение поступит. К примеру, улучшенный бонус, позволяет уничтожить не одну горизонтальную линию, а три. Ну и в игре есть классические бонусы, такие как бомбы разной мощности и пр. Реализованы бонусы не плохо, но у некоторых игроков может возникнуть ощущения их однотипности, к примеру, бонусы серии «маленькая/средняя/большая бомба». Ну, наверно можно и так сказать, но мне понравился сам игровой процесс, а так как игра довольно лёгкая, я не особо замечал однообразие этих бонусов. Честно сказать я не совсем понимаю, почему некоторые игроки не довольны, казалось бы, классической игрой три-в-ряд. Такое чувство, что они ожидали нечто большее, чем три-в-ряд, но этот тип игр и не бывает радикально другим. Так что…это просто хорошо сделанная, без радикализма, без чего-то сверхнового миниатюрная игра (возможно сделанная вообще одним человеком) жанра три-в-ряд. Любителям этого жанра определённо советую.

REVIEW #115
Spooky Bonus
----------

[NOTE: An addendum was added after receiving developer feedback which brought some context to the experience that I was had with this game while evaluating it. The addendum can be found at the bottom of this review.]

*** ORIGINAL REVIEW***
The "match-3" casual game formula has been done and redone hundreds or maybe even thousands of times over. At this point in time, it's really difficult to innovate with this type of title since so many of them exist, some trying to do something different and some just copying from other games or sources. It seems easier (and maybe even wiser) to create a game that's a good mixture of elements that other match-3 titles have tried, and if those elements are balanced well during development, then a fun casual game may be the result.

That introduction is the best way that I know of to describe Spooky Bonus. It's got elements that have been in match-3 titles before: blocks that need matches occurring over them multiple times, special items that can destroy blocks in varying ranges and shapes, super powers that charge up when matching certain items, in-game currency that can be used to purchase upgrades.... the list goes on. However, Spooky Bonus manages to piece all of these elements together into a really fun casual puzzle game. No part of the gameplay experience offered here feels unfair or annoying, and I actually found this title to be pretty addictive.

Spooky Bonus's spooky-yet-family-friendly presentation is decent but not great However, all of the pieces and parts do work together well thematically. The graphics and visuals have that typical "casual game" aesthetic, and the sound effects, while serviceable overall, feature a couple that seem like they were lifted from other, unrelated titles. The music is good and features tracks that almost seem to have their own, individual vibe: one track sounds reminiscent of 1990s Castlevania games, while another almost sounds like it came from a family Halloween movie. The game also features timed and untimed modes, the latter probably being great for children to play and enjoy. However, for anyone that would like a fair challenge, I highly recommend timed mode.

The only complaint that I have is that the game feels a bit short, but otherwise, I was very surprised with how much enjoyment I got out of Spooky Bonus. Some might balk at the $10 USD (current) price point, but I recommend at least picking this up on sale if casual puzzle games are your thing.


***ADDENDUM***
One thing that I neglected to account for in my original review was the time of this game's release, which brings a lot of context to the experience offered here. I had commented that many features in Spooky Bonus could be found in other games nowadays, but that didn't account for the fact that the game was released back in 2013, when such features in match-3 games were either new or much less common-place. Additionally, this release date rules out the possibility that I had heard some of this game's sound effects from other titles made by other developers, as the games that I had in mind were released much later.

Spooky Bonus is a Halloween themed match-3 that I like to play around spooky season. Unlike other match 3 games I've enjoyed, this one has stacking objectives that increase the difficulty throughout the game.  For example, you might be tasked with clearing the board of gold tiles or matching a specific thing so many times. The shape of the board and the various 'obstacles' that appear in later stages force you to think on your feet in the game's 'timed' mode, which counts as a normal/hard difficulty.  Fortunately you have a huge variety of bonus powers you can use to help get rid of obstacles while you play.  Sometimes you will get frustrated with running out of time, but often the way forward is to cleverly make use of these powers.

I know it seems like one of those cheap cell-phone titles, but I've actually found a lot to enjoy here and the main game is pretty solid in terms of how much content it has. I don't know if it has much replayability beyond that, but I'm satisfied with what I've had so far, and all my hours as of this writing have been spent clearing the campaign (I'm not done yet).  I was pleasantly surprised by this title, and recommend it to people looking for a match-3 title with some substance to it.

Nice little game. Pros: All 100 levels are relatively easy to beat (also in timed mode) but not to the point where the game 'plays itself' (as I have experienced with other match 3 games). So I would say the difficulty level is nicely set. The artwork is nice enough and fits the game well. Also, I like the choice of icons for the different pieces.  Match 3 gameplay is good as moving around the pieces is smooth and easy. It even allows for some fast little changes, while more pieces are falling, which makes it more fun because you can sometimes improve your game by fast and smart little adjustments. There are also various tile locks (stone, cobwebs etc.) that you have to blast away or match next to, and I think such tile locks are a nice feature in any match 3 game. The game also has achievements which is another plus - and trading cards if you are into those.

I can only think of two cons: One is that I got a bit tired of the music after some time, because it calls for attention as when a movie reaches a climax. For background music that repeats itself, this is too intense and I would have preferred something more subtle. However, music can be turned off in the settings so that you are not stuck with it if you don't want to. The other is a minor one, but has to do with the items you can purchase. The progression is very straight forward (play the game to get gold - then use gold to buy stuff) but ended up feeling a little superfluous because you need to buy even the decorations you don't particularly like if you want to improve your power-ups. 

Overall I enjoyed this game and - having tried various match 3 games - this definitely deserves recommendation due to the nicely balanced match 3 gameplay.

Отличная игра 3 в ряд, зарабатываем монетки и украшаем дом.

Most people who have a lengthy history of playing games online have undoubtedly played a Match-3 game at some point.  It's probably unnecessary to explain the concept, but the object is to repeatedly find at least three (four or five is also possible) of various items in rows or columns until you reach a goal or you run out of time (depending on the game).  A Match-3 is not the type of game I generally enjoy playing for a long period of time as things can become monotonous fairly quickly, but [i]Spooky Bonus[/i] is not your typical Match-3, as time just seemed to fly by while I was playing it.

[i]Spooky Bonus[/i] has a spooky (that shouldn't come as a surprise) seasonal kind of theme that lends itself to being most popular in late October; that said, the imagery is at best extremely mild when it comes to being dark or scary, and it shouldn't be of great concern if that sort of thing troubles you.  The aforementioned time of year is a big deal to some people (which is fine, people have the right to enjoy whatever traditions and what not), but it just doesn't mean anything to me at this point in my life (you can call me a stick in the mud or something like that).  That might seem like pointless information, but I only say that since I could have played this game in January or May, and it would have been just as much fun for me.  I happened to see a friend playing it recently, and that inspired me to give it a go since I was looking for something different to play for a change, and the game had been sitting in my library for three years.  It took less than 10 minutes to install the game, which was a promising sign from the outset.

Helpful tips are provided early on in the game, and it's very easy to quickly get into the flow of things.  A story isn't a necessity for this type of game, but there is a fairly simple one that fits the theme of [i]Spooky Bonus[/i] as you progress through 100 levels on either relaxed or timed modes.  100 levels might seem like a tall order for a Match-3, but I was surprised at how often I wanted to go for "one more level" instead of just quitting after a short session.  This led to me putting in just over 16 hours in less than a week's time, during which I was able to finish all 100 levels and earn all of the achievements.  The difficulty increases as you progress through the game, but you also gain a total of six unique bonus abilities at various stages that will help you a great deal; that said, you must choose your spots wisely as it takes some time for a given bonus ability to recharge once you have used it.  You will earn most of the achievements if you just put in the time to finish the game, although finishing the game in timed mode (you only have to finish level 100 in that mode for the achievement) might take at least a few tries if you have played the game in its entirety in relaxed mode.  There is one achievement ("Insane Reaction") that was a bit tricky for me, but it's definitely not an insurmountable problem if you can cluster a number of bonus items together and set them off all at once.  The various bonus items are acquired from putting together larger combos (fours or fives, matching a column and a row simultaneously, etc.), and they fill a single spot on the board; the bonus items are separate from the six bonus abilities/power-ups.

I had a blast playing [i]Spooky Bonus[/i], and I highly recommend it to anyone who has even a passing interest in Match-3s; the "very positive" aggregate review score for this game isn't an aberration, as this game is top notch for the genre.  The graphics are very good for a Match-3, and I found the music to be very enjoyable throughout the game.  I generally wait for sales before I purchase many games, and it was no different with [i]Spooky Bonus[/i] as I bought it when there was a 70% off discount in 2019.  It was a huge bargain at that price, and I would have no reservation with recommending the game at full price; it was that enjoyable for me.

[i]Spooky Bonus[/i] may have been designed with a specific time of year in mind, but, if you're looking for a Match-3 that will surprise you with how much time you spend playing it in any given session, it's well worth playing at any time of the year.

This is a cute little Halloween-themed match-3 game.

It offers two modes: timed and relaxed. You’ll need to fully play through the game twice – once in each mode – to get all achievements, but I found the timer to be incredibly generous.

There are 100 different levels. They follow a linear progression, and while you can go back and replay earlier ones, you earn nothing from doing so.

The match-3 gameplay is fairly standard, with classic obstacles like irregular board layouts, layered tiles, destructible blocks, webs, and special tokens that need to be dropped to the bottom. 

Making larger matches spawns one-use powerups on the board. Over the course of the game, you will also unlock and upgrade six different rechargeable tools that will help you clear obstacles faster.
Additionally, you are allowed to swap pieces into an empty space, giving you greater flexibility for matchmaking. 

There were only two aspects I wasn’t entirely fond of:
1) Instead of auto-shuffling the board when you have no more available moves, it treats the board as failed. Luckily that only happened to me once.
2) There are not enough music tracks, and one of the main songs sounds like a low-effort Star Wars rip-off.

Aside from that, though, the game is solid. I didn’t encounter any bugs, and the graphics and interface were crisp.

I got the game on sale for 75% off, and I definitely feel like I got my money’s worth, as it took me about 17 hours to earn all achieves.
